# Every consumer dist/esm build fails on a computed root no workspace can supply

## Context

`npm run build-dist-esm` cannot succeed in any consuming workspace. It fails on a `computed-root` report for a directory the workspace has no reason to own, emitted for a code branch that cannot execute there.

Found while building the real-engine fixture for #17931 — the first thing that has ever run this build from outside this repository. Measured on `dev @ f189cc6ffa`, engine installed into a `mkdtemp` workspace, `buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs` run for real. Full matrix: #17931 (comment `5483577069`).

## The Problem

#17921 added `findUnresolvableImports`, which refuses to let the build exit 0 while an emitted import does not resolve. It has three arms; the `computed-root` arm handles specifiers like `` `../../examples/${path.slice(9)}.mjs` `` — a template literal names no single file, so the arm resolves the literal prefix and asks whether that *directory* is in the output tree. Its stated purpose:

> *"The interpolation is never resolved — only the path before it. A whole source root is likely uncopied."*

That inference holds inside this repository, where `apps/`, `docs/`, `examples/` and `src/` are all default source roots and all present. It does not hold for a consumer, where the same absence means the opposite: the directory is missing because the branch reading it is one this workspace never takes.

Measured residuals for a workspace with the engine installed and its deps hoisted, after clearing every blocker a consumer *can* clear:

```
dist/esm/src/Main.mjs       → ../../../src/main/addon/${i.substring(3)}.mjs  (directory src/main/addon/ is absent)
dist/esm/src/Main.mjs       → ../../../src/main/addon/${e.substring(3)}.mjs  (directory src/main/addon/ is absent)
dist/esm/src/worker/Data.mjs → ../../examples/${e.slice(9)}.mjs              (directory dist/esm/examples/ is absent)
dist/esm/src/worker/Data.mjs → ../../docs/app/${e.slice(9)}.mjs              (directory dist/esm/docs/app/ is absent)
```

Each traces to a guarded branch:

- `src/worker/Data.mjs` `importAppSpaceModule` — `if (path.startsWith('examples/'))` and `if (path.startsWith('docs/app/'))`. A workspace app requests neither.
- `src/Main.mjs` `importAddon` / `onDomContentLoaded` — the `if (addon.startsWith('WS/'))` branch. A workspace declaring no `WS/` addon never enters it.

**`examples/` is decisive on its own.** For a consumer `resolveSourceRoots` returns `['apps', 'docs', 'node_modules/neo.mjs/src', 'src']` — `examples` is not among them, so `dist/esm/examples/` cannot exist unless the workspace declares `neo.esmSourceRoots: ['examples']`, a root it has no reason to own and no documentation tells it to add. Every consumer build fails on that one line. The other three are conditional on workspace shape; this one is unconditional.

Confirmed by construction: adding `neo.esmSourceRoots: ['examples']` plus a `docs/` root and a `src/main/addon/` directory is what finally took the build to exit 0 — four appeasements, none of which a real workspace would author.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/esmDistTransforms.mjs` — `findUnresolvableImports` classifies `missing` / `computed-root` / `engine-identity`; `computedSpecifierRoot` truncates at the first interpolation.
- `buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs` — reports the three classes separately, then `if (unresolvable.length > 0) process.exit(1)` treats all three as equally fatal.
- `resolveSourceRoots` in the same module owns the consumer default set that makes `examples/` unreachable.

The `missing` arm is unaffected and remains the load-bearing one: a *literal* specifier that does not resolve is a real dangling import regardless of who is building, and it is what catches an uncopied root for any module actually imported statically.

## The Fix

The build must stop treating `computed-root` as fatal, keeping it as a diagnostic. A computed specifier names no module; the arm cannot distinguish an uncopied source root from a branch this workspace does not take, and one of those two readings is wrong on every consumer build while the other has never once fired here on a real defect.

Concretely: exclude `computed-root` from the exit-1 set in `buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs`, keep its `console.error` block, and reword it as a warning that names both readings instead of asserting the uncopied-root one.

The alternative — teaching the arm which computed roots are conditional — is rejected under **Avoided Traps** below.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. This narrows a guard introduced by #17921; no ADR governs the `dist/esm` resolution guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A workspace with the engine installed, its deps hoisted, no `examples/` and no `src/main/addon/`, and **no `neo.esmSourceRoots` declaration**, builds `dist/esm` to exit 0.
- [ ] The `computed-root` report still prints, naming each specifier and its truncated root, and states both readings rather than asserting the uncopied-root one.
- [ ] The `missing` arm still fails the build: a literal specifier that does not resolve exits 1, proven by a mutation that re-introduces one.
- [ ] The `engine-identity` arm still fails the build, proven the same way.
- [ ] The existing arms in `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/esmWorkspaceBuild.spec.mjs` that assert exit 1 on an undeclared source root keep passing. Checked before filing rather than left as a risk: that case reports under `do not resolve inside the output tree`, i.e. the `missing` arm, so narrowing `computed-root` does not reach it.

## Out of Scope

- The `WS/` addon path resolving outside `dist/esm` — a separate runtime defect, filed alongside this one.
- The parse5 copy site, fixed under #17931.
- Dependency resolution by filesystem path — #17868.
- Any change to `resolveSourceRoots`' default set.

## Avoided Traps

**Adding `examples` to the consumer default roots.** It would clear the decisive symptom and be wrong: a consumer has no `examples/` tree, so the root would be copied as empty or skipped, and the other three reports would survive untouched.

**Teaching the guard which computed roots are conditional** — a list of "these branches are optional". That list is a second copy of control flow already expressed in `Data.mjs` and `Main.mjs`, and it goes stale the first time either grows a branch. The guard would then be confidently wrong instead of noisily right.

**Leaving it and documenting the workaround.** Four appeasement steps stand between a generated workspace and a working `dist/esm` build, none discoverable from the error text. A build every consumer must be told how to trick is not a guard.

## Related

- #17921 — introduced the guard.
- #17931 — the real-engine fixture that surfaced this; carries the full measurement matrix.

- `.github/workflows/consumer-runtime-build.yml` — the sibling guard that builds from outside for the webpack targets, and the reason this class is known.
